title: How to Export Advanced Hunting Results from Microsoft Defender XDR
content_md: Run your query in Advanced hunting , then send the same query to Microsoft Graph’s runHuntingQuery to get the results as JSON. The portal’s export button produces a spreadsheet-style file that LogTotal doesn’t read today. Advanced hunting keeps 30 days of data, so anything older has to come from Sentinel or wherever you stream Defender data. Defender XDR holds endpoint, identity, email and cloud app telemetry in one queryable place, which makes it the first stop in most Microsoft-shop investigations. Prime Core has 17,197 detection rules for Microsoft Defender data, mapped to 659 MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Below is how to pull a slice out, sanitize it, and investigate it for free in LogTotal. Get Started For Free Before you start Permissions. For Graph, you need the ThreatHunting.Read.All permission. The signed-in user also needs a Defender role that allows advanced hunting. Limits. Queries time out after a few minutes, and results are capped. Plan to split by time or by device. The tables. DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceNetworkEvents, DeviceLogonEvents, DeviceFileEvents, DeviceRegistryEvents, DeviceEvents (a mixed bag, including ASR and AMSI events), EmailEvents, IdentityLogonEvents, and AlertInfo with AlertEvidence. The time column is Timestamp. The examples follow Microsoft’s documentation, checked October 2026. Step 1: Write the query DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp between (datetime(2026-10-19) .. datetime(2026-10-20)) | where DeviceName startswith "ws-042" | project Tim
